title: Does setting foam up stomp on an existing git hook?
body:
`foam init` and `foam sync --setup` call `install_hook` in `src/cmd.rs`, which writes the pre-push hook that pushes the data ref. What it does with a hook that is already there, read from the code at c15fa5e:

| found | what happens |
|---|---|
| `core.hooksPath` set | nothing is written; stderr prints the block to add by hand |
| a hook with foam's marker line | nothing |
| a hook whose shebang is not a shell | left alone; stderr prints the block to run from it |
| any other hook | foam's block is appended after the existing text |
| no hook | foam's script is written, mode 755 |

`tests/cli.rs` covers the `core.hooksPath` case, the non-shell case and the append. So on what is written, the answer is no: an existing hook keeps its text.

`foam setup claude` edits `.claude/settings.json` through `serde_json`, adds its own entry to the `hooks` object and removes only entries it recognises as its own, so other hooks in that file stay.

## Open

- An existing hook that ends in `exec` or `exit` before its last line never reaches foam's block, so foam's push of the data ref silently does not happen. `install_hook` does not look for that, and nothing tells the user. Whether to detect it, or to put foam's block first, is the question that needs an answer.
- `serde_json` rewrites `.claude/settings.json` whole. Whether the user's key order and formatting survive depends on the `preserve_order` feature, which needs checking.
- The append sets the hook's mode to 755 whatever it was before.
